Which statement about the waves emitted by the loudspeakers is not a necessary condition for
the microphone to detect a fixed point along the line where there is no sound?

options.A: The waves must be emitted in phase.
options.B: The waves must be emitted with a similar amplitude.
options.C: The waves must have the same frequency.
options.D: The waves must have the same wavelength.

stem:
Two waves, each with a constant amplitude, interfere and produce an interference pattern. The
pattern has minima at fixed points where the displacement is zero at all times.
Which statement describes the two waves?

options.A: They must be coherent and of the same amplitude.
options.B: They must be coherent but not necessarily of the same amplitude.
options.C: They must be of the same amplitude but not necessarily coherent.
options.D: They must not be coherent or of the same amplitude.

options.C: There is a constant non-zero difference in frequency of the two waves at Z.

stem:
In a dark room, a small source of red light illuminates two slits that are 0.75 mm apart. A few
metres beyond the slits, the light falls on a screen producing a series of equally spaced bright
lines.
Which change would cause the distance between the bright lines on the screen to be reduced?

options.A: Change the source for one emitting blue light.
options.B: Reduce the distance between the light source and the slits.
options.C: Reduce the distance between the slits to 0.55 mm.
options.D: Reduce the intensity of the light source.

Why can an observable interference pattern never be obtained between two monochromatic
beams of light from different lamps?

options.A: The frequency of the light from the two lamps can never be the same.
options.B: The light from the two lamps can never be coherent.
options.C: The temperature of the filaments of the two lamps used can never be the same.
options.D: The wavelength of the light from the two lamps must always be different.
